bio.#cdata-section:
Jacob Abel competed in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in 2026 for the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500, driving the No. 51 Chevrolet for Abel Motorsports and his father, Bill Abel. He made his debut in the series in 2025 with Dale Coyne Racing, posting a career-best 11th at Iowa Speedway.

A product of the INDYCAR development ladder, he finished second in INDY NXT by Firestone in 2024, earning three wins and three poles with his family-run team. Away from the track, he enjoys cycling and lacrosse – a sport he played in high school – along with skiing, tennis and golf. He attended Butler University in Indianapolis.

Marcus Armstrong completed his second season with Meyer Shank Racing in 2026, driving the No. 66 Honda. The 2023 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Rookie of the Year spent two seasons with Chip Ganassi Racing before moving to MSR under a technical partnership. In 2025, he recorded a career-best championship finish of eighth overall and tied his best race result with a third-place finish at Iowa.

Armstrong will move to the No. 60 Honda for Meyer Shank Racing in 2027.

A native of New Zealand, Armstrong won five karting championships before racing in FIA F3, where he earned four wins, four poles and 16 podiums over two seasons. He also won the 2017 Italian F4 championship and finished second in ADAC F4 the same year. Prior to switching to INDYCAR, he competed in FIA F2 for three seasons, earning four wins.

Off track, Armstrong enjoys all things sports and competition, particularly tennis matches with his younger brother and watching the NFL. He is training to break the world record in planking, though that may be a work in progress. He is an avid sneakerhead with an extensive collection and prefers listening to podcasts over music.

The Hoosier-born Ed Carpenter is a staple of the INDYCAR paddock, racing for more than 23 years and currently the only owner/driver in the field. He competes exclusively in the Indianapolis 500, where he has claimed three poles in 2013, 2014 and 2018, driving the No. 33 Chevrolet.

In 2003, Carpenter won the first INDY NXT by Firestone race at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. His INDYCAR SERIES career includes three wins, four poles and nine podiums, with his first NTT INDYCAR SERIES victory coming in 2011 at Kentucky.

A graduate of Butler University in Indianapolis, Carpenter is a fan of the Butler Bulldogs men’s basketball team, the Indiana Pacers and Indianapolis Colts. He earned his pilot license and often flies himself to races with Alexander Rossi. He and his wife, Heather, have three children.

A member of the illustrious “club” of four-time Indianapolis 500 winners, Helio Castroneves completed his 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season with Meyer Shank Racing, piloting the No. 06 Honda in the 110th Running of The Greatest Spectacle in Racing.

Castroneves has 31 wins and 50 poles, with his first race win coming in the 2000 season. His racing career also includes wins in IMSA, where he was part of the winning Rolex 24 At Daytona for three consecutive years, and he won the 2020 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship title in the Daytona International Prototype class.

Beyond motorsports, Castroneves is also a champion on the dance floor, winning Season 5 of “Dancing with the Stars” in 2007.

Caio Collet completed his rookie season with AJ Foyt Racing in 2026, driving the No. 4 Chevrolet. He graduated from INDY NXT by Firestone after finishing second in the 2025 standings and continued his progression to the highest level of North American open-wheel racing.

In 2025, Collet won two INDY NXT races and three poles. Over his INDY NXT career, he earned Rookie of the Year honors in 2024 and captured three wins and four poles overall. Internationally, he won the 2018 French F4 Championship and finished runner-up in the 2020 Formula Renault Eurocup. He has also served as a Nissan Formula E reserve driver.

Off track, Collet is passionate about racing and cherishes his upbringing in Sao Paulo, including its diverse food culture and social life. He is inspired by mentors Tony Kanaan and fellow Brazilian Helio Castroneves.

Conor Daly competed in the 2026 Indianapolis 500 with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing, driving the No. 23 Chevrolet. He will return to full-time competition with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing in partnership with Honda in 2027, as the team returns to the grid for its first full season since 2012.

Daly won the 2010 Star Mazda title with Juncos Racing and has victories in both Star Mazda (now USF Pro 2000) and Indy Lights. Daly has tested an F1 car for Force India, won in GP3 at Barcelona, and was the inaugural MRF Challenge Series champion in India. He has also competed in NASCAR’s three national series.

A second-generation racer, he is the son of former Formula One and INDYCAR driver Derek Daly. He hosts the Speed Street podcast for Dale Earnhardt Jr.’s Dirty Mo Media.

Scott Dixon completed his 26th season in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and 25th with Chip Ganassi Racing, driving the No. 9 Honda.

The 46-year-old New Zealander is a six-time series champion (2003, 2008, 2013, 2015, 2018, 2020) and 2008 Indianapolis 500 winner. He holds the most wins of any active driver with 59 and set the all-time record for series starts in 2025. Dixon began his career in Formula Ford, Toyota Atlantic and Indy Lights before joining INDYCAR in 2001 with PacWest Racing.

Off track, he is married to Emma, a former track champion, and has three children — Poppy, Tilly and Kit. Dixon was inducted into the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America in 2024 and knighted by New Zealand in 2025.

Dixon will move to Arrow McLaren for the 2027 season.

Marcus Ericsson completed his third season with Andretti Global in 2026, earning his first win with the team on the streets of Markham, Ontario in the No. 28 Honda. The 36-year-old Swedish driver won the 2022 Indianapolis 500 with Chip Ganassi Racing.

Ericsson competed in Formula 1 for five seasons with Sauber (2015–2018) before joining the NTT INDYCAR SERIES with Arrow Schmidt Peterson Motorsports in 2019. He has also won championships in British Formula BMW and Japanese F3 and competed in British F3 and FIA Formula 2. After finishing sixth in the standings in 2021, 2022 and 2023, he had a challenging 2025 season, ending 20th in the points.

In 2025, Ericsson married his wife, Iris. The couple enjoys traveling and fashion. He is also a fan of professional hockey, cheering for Sweden, and his favorite foods include Mexican and Japanese cuisine.

Santino Ferrucci, the 2019 Indianapolis 500 Rookie of the Year, completed his fourth consecutive season with AJ Foyt Racing in the No. 14 Chevrolet. The 2026 season marked his sixth full-time season and ninth overall in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

At 16, Ferrucci became the youngest winner of a British Formula 3 race and later competed in GP3 (now FIA Formula 3) and FIA Formula 2 before returning to the U.S. in 2018 to race in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and NASCAR. He has also competed multiple times in the Chili Bowl Midget Nationals. In 2025, he finished 16th in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES standings, with a best finish of second at Detroit; his career-best points finish was ninth in 2024.

Off track, Ferrucci enjoys golf, online gaming and restoring go-karts, including two he still owns from his early racing days. Featured in GQ Magazine at age 11 as a karting prodigy, the Connecticut native now resides in Dallas, Texas, and lists steak and Italian cuisine among his favorite foods.

Louis Foster completed his second NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026, driving the No. 45 Honda for Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing. The 2025 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Rookie of the Year earned his second NTT P1 Award in 2026 on the streets of Markham, Ontario.

Before moving to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in 2025, Foster was the 2024 INDY NXT by Firestone champion with Andretti Global, claiming eight wins, 12 podiums and six poles. He previously captured the 2022 Indy Pro 2000 championship and was a finalist for the Autosport BRDC Award. Foster began karting at age nine, winning club championships at Camberley Kart Club and Forest Edge Kart Club in 2013 and 2015.

Hailing from Odiham, England, Foster now resides in Indianapolis. He is the son of former British Touring Car Championship racer Nick Foster and enjoys watching racing — particularly past INDYCAR SERIES events, Formula 1 and BTCC — and following friends competing globally. Off track, he enjoys the gym, sim racing and cycling; in 2017, he rode across Snowdonia and the Brecon Beacons to raise funds for CRY.

Romain Grosjean completed his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026 with Dale Coyne Racing, driving the No. 18 Honda. After spending 2025 as a reserve driver with PREMA Racing, he resumed full-time competition with the team where he made his INDYCAR debut in 2021, earning a podium finish on the streets of Markham, Ontario.

The Swiss-born French driver made 180 Formula 1 starts, earning 10 podium finishes, including career-best runner-up results in Montreal and Austin, Texas. Since transitioning to INDYCAR, Grosjean has competed for Dale Coyne Racing, Andretti Global and Juncos Hollinger Racing, establishing himself as a versatile contender across street circuits, road courses and ovals.

Off track, Grosjean speaks French, English and Italian. He is passionate about cooking and has said he would have pursued a career as a chef if racing hadn’t worked out. He and his wife, Marion, have co-authored a cookbook.

A two-time INDY NXT by Firestone championship runner-up, British driver Jack Harvey competed in the 2026 Indianapolis 500 with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing, driving the No. 24 Chevrolet.

Harvey has lived in both the United States and France but has remained grounded in his sense of home – the small village of Bassingham in Lincolnshire, England. He is among the drivers who have won on both the oval and road courses at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, with wins on both circuits in 2015 while racing in INDY NXT. Harvey has 10 racing championship wins in his career, including the British Formula 3 title in 2012.

Away from the track, Harvey enjoys baking, target shooting, watching Star Wars and Marvel movies, and watching soccer and American football.

Dennis Hauger completed his rookie NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026, driving the No. 19 Honda for Dale Coyne Racing in technical partnership with Andretti Global. The Norwegian earned Rookie of the Year honors in his debut season, besting Mick Schumacher and Caio Collet.

Hauger has a decorated junior career, winning the 2021 FIA Formula 3 championship. In 2025, he dominated INDY NXT by Firestone with Andretti Global, earning six wins, eight poles and the championship over Collet by 72 points. Hauger is nicknamed the “Norwegian Nightmare.”

Off track, he enjoys running, working out, simulator training and any activity that sharpens his driving skills.

In 2026, Ryan Hunter-Reay raced a one-off entry in the Indianapolis 500 with Arrow McLaren, driving the No. 31 Chevrolet. He was named Sporting Director for Arrow McLaren in June and will return with the team for the 111th Running of the Indianapolis 500 in 2027.

The 45-year-old Floridian is an 18-time winner in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, capturing the championship in 2012 with Andretti Global and winning the 2014 Indianapolis 500. He is the only American driver to record victories in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, CART, Champ Car, American Le Mans Series and Grand-Am Rolex Sports Car Series. Hunter-Reay has also represented Team USA eight times at the Race of Champions, beginning in 2012 following his INDYCAR SERIES championship.

Off the track, he earned ESPY Awards for Best Driver in 2013 and 2014. Hunter-Reay enjoys deep-sea fishing, scuba diving, free diving and spearfishing. His wife Beccy comes from a racing family – her brother, Robby Gordon, won multiple races in the INDYCAR SERIES, NASCAR Cup Series and rally racing – and their three sons have all started in go-karting.

Kyle Kirkwood completed his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026, continuing with Andretti Global in the No. 27 Honda. The 27-year-old Floridian earned a career-best second-place finish in the championship standings, winning at Arlington and Washington, D.C.

Kirkwood advanced through the open-wheel ladder with championships in USF2000 (2018), USF Pro 2000 (2019) and INDY NXT by Firestone (2021). Since joining Andretti Global in 2023, he has been one of the series’ most dominant drivers on street circuits, earning the nickname "King of the Streets" for his success.

Off track, Kirkwood enjoys deep-sea fishing, diving, surfing, golf and pickleball, continually pushing himself to improve in all aspects of life.

driver.name: Katherine Legge
driver.team: HMD Motorsports w/ AJ Foyt Racing

bio.#cdata-section:
Katherine Legge rejoined the NTT INDYCAR SERIES for the 110th Indianapolis 500 in 2026, driving the No. 11 Chevrolet for HMD Motorsports with AJ Foyt Racing.

She started competing in Champ Car in 2006 before making multiple starts in the INDYCAR SERIES and the Indianapolis 500. A fan favorite across the world known for her motorsports versatility and persistence, Legge became one of the few women to race at Indy, and currently holds the fastest qualifying speed by a woman at the Indianapolis 500 in 2023.

Christian Lundgaard, the 2022 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Rookie of the Year, completed his second season with Arrow McLaren in 2026, driving the No. 7 Chevrolet. He earned two victories, at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course and Road America, along with multiple podium finishes. He became only the sixth driver in series history to complete 100% of the season’s laps and finished a career-best third in the championship standings.

Before joining Arrow McLaren, Lundgaard competed for Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing, earning his first NTT INDYCAR SERIES victory at Toronto in 2023. He also competed in FIA Formula 2, recording two wins and six podium finishes in 2020. Earlier in his career, he captured championships in SMP F4 and Spanish F4 and earned an FIA Formula 3 race victory.

Born in Denmark, Lundgaard is the son of European Rally champion Henrik Lundgaard. He began racing alongside his older brother, Daniel, in karting, winning Danish and European karting titles. Away from the track, Lundgaard enjoys golf, playing Call of Duty on his PlayStation and watching Netflix shows, particularly NCIS.

David Malukas completed his first season with Team Penske in 2026, driving the No. 12 Chevrolet. He finished runner-up to Felix Rosenqvist in the 2026 Indianapolis 500 in the closest finish in race history, earning a career-best championship finish of fifth.

A 24-year-old INDY NXT by Firestone graduate, Malukas finished second in the standings in 2021 after a record 16 podiums. He previously drove for Dale Coyne Racing, Meyer Shank Racing and AJ Foyt Racing before joining Team Penske.

Malukas is a first-generation Lithuanian-American, the only son of immigrants Henry and Daiva, who own INDY NXT by Firestone championship team HMD Motorsports. He grew up in southwest Chicago, moved to Indianapolis in 2024 and relocated to Charlotte, North Carolina in 2026.

Off the track, he enjoys gaming, memes and hi-fidelity music.

Scott McLaughlin completed his sixth NTT INDYCAR SERIES season with Team Penske in 2026, driving the No. 3 Chevrolet. He finished sixth in the standings, ending a 35-race winless drought with a victory in the season finale at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.

McLaughlin owns Team Penske’s all-time poles record, and his first career NTT INDYCAR SERIES win came in 2022 at St. Petersburg. He has a career-best points finish of third in both 2023 and 2024.

Off track, McLaughlin is married to Karly, and they welcomed their daughter Lucy in October 2024. He earned American citizenship in 2025 and enjoys American football, iRacing, puzzles, music, traveling and golf. A fan of the Carolina Panthers (NFL), Wisconsin Badgers (NCAA), New York Knicks (NBA) and New York Rangers (NHL), he has played some of the sport’s most notable courses, including Augusta National, Pebble Beach, Bay Hill and Whistling Straits.

Josef Newgarden completed his 15th NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026 and his 10th consecutive season with Team Penske, driving the No. 2 Chevrolet. The 35-year-old two-time series champion and two-time Indianapolis 500 winner finished seventh in the standings, earning victories at Phoenix and World Wide Technology Raceway.

He won back-to-back Indianapolis 500s in 2023 and 2024, becoming the first driver to do so since Helio Castroneves in 2001–2002.

With 34 career wins, Newgarden is the winningest active American driver in the series. A graduate of INDY NXT by Firestone, the Nashville, Tennessee, native won the 2011 championship with five victories.

Off the track, Newgarden enjoys traveling with his wife, Ashley, and son, Kota, exploring new cities and cultures. He holds dual citizenship in the United States and Denmark, lived in England from 2009 to 2010, and competed across Europe in Formula Ford and GP3. Newgarden is also the author of two children’s books: Josef, The Indy Car Driver and Josef’s Big Dream: An Indy 500 Story.

Pato O’Ward completed his ninth NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026, returning for his sixth year with Arrow McLaren in the No. 5 Chevrolet. The 27-year-old earned three victories, winning at Mid-Ohio and sweeping the Milwaukee doubleheader to finish fourth in the standings.

Born in Monterrey, Mexico, and raised in San Antonio, Texas, O’Ward now resides in Indianapolis. An INDY NXT by Firestone graduate and series champion, he rose through the development ladder before establishing himself as a consistent front-runner in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. He also has served as a reserve driver for the McLaren Formula 1 Team and won the 2017 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship Prototype Challenge title, along with two class victories at the Rolex 24 at Daytona and a Prototype Challenge class win at the 12 Hours of Sebring.

Off the track, O’Ward focuses on boxing and weight training and is a self-proclaimed foodie who enjoys chilaquiles and sushi. His Corgi, Norbi, often travels with him to races.

Alex Palou is a five-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion (2021, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026) and winner of the 109th Indianapolis 500. In 2026, he became just the second driver in INDYCAR SERIES history to win four consecutive championships, joining only Sébastien Bourdais. Palou’s historic season included six victories, eight poles and 15 top-10 finishes in 18 races.

Driving the No. 10 Honda for Chip Ganassi Racing, 29-year-old Palou has also competed and won in Euroformula Open, Spanish Formula 3, GP3, Japanese Formula 3 and Super Formula, where he earned 2019 Rookie of the Year honors.

Off the track, Palou speaks Spanish, English and Italian, plays pickleball, and enjoys sports, outdoor activities and music. He co-owns Palou Motorsports with his father and is married to Esther, with whom he has a daughter, Lucia.

Will Power joined Andretti Global for the 2026 season, driving the No. 26 Honda. The 45-year-old Toowoomba, Australia, native competed in his 19th NTT INDYCAR SERIES season and first with Andretti Global, following a 17-year tenure with Team Penske.

Power holds the all-time INDYCAR SERIES record for pole positions with 71, surpassing Mario Andretti in 2022, and ranks fourth on the all-time wins list with 45 career victories. A two-time series champion (2014, 2022) and 2018 Indianapolis 500 winner, he finished 11th in the 2026 standings with five podium finishes, bringing extensive experience to Andretti Global’s lineup.

Off the track, Power and his wife, Elizabeth, welcomed their son, Beau, in 2016. He enjoys playing drums, a hobby he began at age 15, and maintains a rigorous training regimen that includes swimming, cycling, weightlifting and rowing. Power is also deeply involved in karting, mentoring young drivers, including INDY NXT by Firestone’s Myles Rowe.

Graham Rahal completed his 20th season in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, returning to Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing in the No. 15 Honda. He recorded three podium finishes in 2026 for the team co-owned by his father, 1986 Indianapolis 500 winner Bobby Rahal, David Letterman and businessman Mike Lanigan.

The Ohio native made his INDYCAR debut at age 18 and became the second-youngest race winner in series history at St. Petersburg in 2008, followed by becoming the second-youngest pole winner at the same venue in 2009. He continues to be one of the longest-tenured drivers in the series.

Off track, Rahal is married to retired drag racing star Courtney Force and is the father of three daughters. He founded the Graham and Courtney Rahal Foundation, which has donated more than $2 million to support veterans, cancer research, and family-focused causes. An avid golfer, he is also a passionate fan of Ohio State football and the NHL’s Columbus Blue Jackets.

Outside of INDYCAR, Rahal owns multiple businesses including Graham Rahal Performance, Rahal Ducati dealerships, Rahal Paint Protection and Rahal Piaggio, and he fields a Ducati Supersport team in MotoAmerica.

Christian Rasmussen completed his first full NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2025 with ECR and returned to drive the No. 21 Chevrolet in 2026. After making 14 starts as a rookie in 2024 following his 2023 INDY NXT by Firestone championship, Rasmussen earned his first career NTT INDYCAR SERIES victory at the Milwaukee Mile in 2025.

The 26-year-old Copenhagen, Denmark, native is just the second driver in history to win a championship at every level feeding into the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, capturing titles in USF2000 (2020), USF Pro 2000 (2021) and INDY NXT (2023). He has shown particular strength on oval tracks, where aggressive strategy and strong racecraft have produced standout results.

Off the track, Rasmussen enjoys playing pickleball with fellow drivers, has a passion for classic cars and describes himself as a “big car guy.” He is close friends with fellow Danish driver Christian Lundgaard and is learning to play golf.

Sting Ray Robb completed his fourth NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026, continuing with Juncos Hollinger Racing for a second consecutive year in the No. 77 Chevrolet. He finished 25th in the championship standings.

Before joining Juncos Hollinger Racing in 2025, Robb competed for Dale Coyne Racing and AJ Foyt Racing.

Robb captured the 2020 USF Pro 2000 championship before advancing to INDY NXT by Firestone, where he finished second in the 2022 standings. His racing background also includes competition in the Formula Car Challenge and the NASCAR K&N Pro Series West.

Yes, Sting Ray is his real name -- inspired by the Corvette. Faith plays a central role in his life, and off the track he enjoys spending time outdoors in Idaho’s mountains, including snow skiing, hunting, water sports and rock climbing.

The 24-year-old American married his wife, Molly, in November 2024 and was a multi-sport athlete in high school, competing in basketball and cross country in Payette, Idaho.

Felix Rosenqvist completed his eighth season in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and third with Meyer Shank Racing in 2026, driving the No. 60 Honda. He captured his first Indianapolis 500 victory in 2026, making a dramatic last-lap pass on David Malukas to win by just 0.0233 of a second — the closest finish in the race's more than century-long history. In 2027, Rosenqvist will return to Arrow McLaren, where he will race alongside Pato O'Ward and Scott Dixon.

Before joining Meyer Shank Racing, Rosenqvist competed for Arrow McLaren from 2021-23 after beginning his INDYCAR career with Chip Ganassi Racing. He earned Rookie of the Year honors in 2019 before scoring his first series victory at Road America the following season.

Prior to INDYCAR, Rosenqvist competed in Formula E, earning race victories while establishing himself among the series' top drivers. He also captured the FIA Formula 3 European championship, won multiple Formula Renault titles and claimed victories in prestigious events including the Masters of Formula 3 and the Macau Grand Prix.

Off track, Rosenqvist married Emille in September 2024 and the couple welcomed their first child, Stella, in May 2026. Known as “FRO,” he enjoys skiing, skateboarding, hiking, video games and music ranging from Slipknot to Coldplay. His racing hero is Mika Häkkinen.

Alexander Rossi completed his 11th season in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and second with ECR in 2026, driving the No. 20 Chevrolet. An eight-time race winner, Rossi recorded his first podium with the team with a third-place finish at the season finale at Laguna Seca.

Rossi moved to Europe at age 17 to pursue a Formula 1 career and made five starts with Manor Marussia in 2015, becoming just the third American driver to race in F1 since 1990. Upon returning to the United States, he joined Andretti Autosport and won the 100th running of the Indianapolis 500 in 2016, becoming the first rookie winner since 2001 and the first American rookie to win since 1928. His résumé also includes wins in the GP2 Series and World Series by Renault, along with starts in the 24 Hours of Le Mans, Rolex 24 at Daytona, Baja 1000 and Bathurst 1000.

Off track, Rossi is married to his wife Kelly, and the couple welcomed their son Benjamin in May 2025. He co-hosts the podcast Off Track with Hinch & Rossi alongside James Hinchcliffe and competed on Season 30 of The Amazing Race with fellow INDYCAR driver Conor Daly. Rossi enjoys skiing, dirt bikes, wakeboarding, cooking, flying as a licensed private pilot, and spending time outdoors with his dogs.

A two-time Indianapolis 500 champion, Takuma Sato returned to Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing in 2026 for the 110th Indianapolis 500, piloting the No. 75 Honda.

Sato was the first Japanese driver to win an INDYCAR SERIES race, winning in Long Beach in 2013, and the first to win the Indianapolis 500 in 2017. Outside of racing, Sato was a national high school cycling champion and still uses cycling as part of his training regimen. The Japanese edition of Esquire magazine named Sato one of The Mavericks of 2019 and the Japanese edition of GQ magazine named him one of the nine “2017 Men of the Year.”

Mick Schumacher completed his first full-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in 2026, driving the No. 47 Honda for Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing. He will move to Meyer Shank Racing in 2027, driving the No. 66 Honda.

The son of seven-time Formula 1 world champion Michael Schumacher, Mick captured the 2018 FIA Formula 3 European Championship and the 2020 FIA Formula 2 Championship. He raced in Formula 1 with Haas from 2021 to 2022, later serving as a reserve driver for Mercedes and McLaren before joining Alpine’s World Endurance Championship program in 2024.

Off track, Schumacher enjoys adrenaline-driven activities, including skydiving, off-roading, rallying, cycling, squash, football and physical training.

Nolan Siegel completed his third season in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES with Arrow McLaren in 2026, continuing in the No. 6 Chevrolet. The 21-year-old from Palo Alto, California, made his series debut midway through the 2024 season.

The 2023 INDY NXT by Firestone Rookie of the Year finished 20th in the 2026 standings, with three top-10 finishes and a career-best sixth-place finish at Washington, D.C. Siegel has earned race wins in INDY NXT and other open-wheel ladder series, while also finding success in sports car competition. In 2024, he co-drove United Autosports’ LMP2 entry to a class victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans and has competed in the Asian Le Mans Series, IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship and World Challenge GT3.

Off track, Siegel has deferred enrollment in Stanford University’s Department of Economics while racing professionally. He enjoys playing guitar, sailing and pursuing his pilot’s license, and is a fan of the San Francisco 49ers, Golden State Warriors and San Jose Sharks.

driver.name: Kyffin Simpson

bio.#cdata-section:
Kyffin Simpson completed his third season with Chip Ganassi Racing in 2026, driving the No. 8 Honda.

The 21-year-old from the Cayman Islands earned his first INDYCAR podium in Toronto in 2025. Across his career, he has won the 2021 Formula Regional Americas championship, the LMP2 title in the European Le Mans Series, and class victories at IMSA’s 12 Hours of Sebring and the Four Hours of Dubai.

Simpson is a graduate of INDY NXT by Firestone, where he raced for two seasons. Off track, he enjoys kitesurfing, surfing, swimming, cycling and training.

driver.residence: Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands / Indianapolis, Indiana

bio.#cdata-section:
Rinus VeeKay completed his first full season with Juncos Hollinger Racing in 2026, driving the No. 76 Chevrolet. He led the team to its best-ever championship finish of 10th, earning its second-ever podium at Milwaukee along with four top-five and eight top-10 finishes.

Prior to joining Juncos Hollinger Racing, VeeKay recorded six top-10 finishes and one podium, finishing second on the Streets of Toronto and 14th in the championship standings with Dale Coyne Racing in 2025.

A graduate of INDY NXT by Firestone, VeeKay was named NTT INDYCAR SERIES Rookie of the Year in 2020 and earned his first career victory at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course in May 2021 with Ed Carpenter Racing. Across USF2000, USF Pro 2000 and INDY NXT, he amassed 16 wins and 36 podiums in 48 starts.

He married longtime partner Carmen in 2023, a professional boxer with an undefeated kickboxing record of 28–0. A devoted athlete, VeeKay trains regularly and enjoys outdoor workouts. He is also an avid fan of internet meme culture and often shares memes with friends.

The 25-year-old from Hoofddorp, Netherlands, resides in Indianapolis.
